one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled event falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29: Q1 FY27 results come after the fiscal quarter ends Oct 31 (Q1 FY26 was reported Nov 20, 2025; an unconfirmed report points to about Dec 1, 2026), and the Sep 17 investor day already reaffirmed guidance. The stock slid from ~$303 after the investor day to $268, ~6% above its 52-week low, so negative momentum and oversold reversal roughly offset. I use a near-symmetric lognormal around $268 at ~14% monthly sigma (50%/3.5) with a very slight negative drift (P(>=268) = 0.49). Mid-October macro prints (CPI, jobs) and software-sector AI headlines are the swing factors. The supervisor's review did not change this; the 1-month ladder moves only marginally.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (FY28E SBC-inclusive EPS $25.5 x 12.5x = $319, weight 0.6) and normalized SBC-burdened FCF yield (FY28E ~$24.4/share at 8% plus ~$3/share of remaining OBBBA cash-tax benefit = $308, weight 0.4) gives ~$315 per share 12 months out (round 1: $334).

Between H&R Block's ~15% earnings yield (6.6x) and a high-quality compounder's ~5%; roughly INTU's current normalized yield (~7.5%), so no re-rating is assumed in this leg.

bear.story: TY2026 season repeats share loss (TurboTax units down again against a growing self-prepared category) as free entry points and AI agents compress price; FY27 EPS misses and FY28 guide is flat at ~$22; the stock de-rates toward an H&R Block-like 7x (~$155-165). A recession (Polymarket ~35% by end-2027, second-hand, thin evidence) would hit QBO/Mailchimp/Credit Karma too.

base.story: Intuit roughly delivers the guide (~$23 EPS, revenue +9-10%), the tax season is 'fine not great' (TurboTax +2-3%), buybacks retire ~4%/yr net, and the multiple recovers only slightly to ~11.5-12x on ~$25.5 NTM EPS.

bull.story: Tax season shows TurboTax units stabilizing with AI-assisted 'done-for-you' lifting ARPU, GBS/Big Bets keep growing mid-teens, and the software sector re-rates as in 2023 after the 2022 crash; multiple returns to ~16x on ~$26.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$195 (~8.5x FY27 guided SBC-inclusive EPS and ~11% normalized SBC-burdened FCF yield) the market would be pricing an earnings decline, not just a de-rating: most likely a failed 2027 tax season (TurboTax units down again vs a growing category), a guide cut at Q2/Q3 FY27, or QuickBooks customer growth turning negative. Lowered from $200 because the H&R Block comparable sits at ~6.6x, so a pure de-rating floor could be ~$150-160; $195 remains the level where fundamentals, not multiple noise, are the likely explanation.

reasoning: Round 2 applies the supervisor's evidence-backed corrections, which I verified: (1) the FY26 8-K cash flow statement shows a +$1.28B deferred income tax add-back (vs -$435M in FY25), so my FCF leg built on $8.8B OCF was overstated; normalized SBC-burdened FCF is ~$5.3B and my FCF leg falls from $338 to $308. (2) H&R Block closed $40.58 on 2026-09-29 (Twelve Data) vs FY27 adj EPS guide $6.04-6.24, i.e. ~6.6x, not 8-9x; my 'practical floor' near $185-205 was too high, and an ex-growth multiple on flat EPS gives ~$150-160, so I cut the bear price to $160 and the P/E multiple to 12.5x. (3) Net buyback accretion is ~4%/yr, not 2%, which I net against the TurboTax share-loss drag to keep FY28 EPS at $25.5. (4) TurboTax units -2% while IRS self-prepared e-file rose 1.7% is share loss in a growing category, which weakens my META/CRM/ADBE 2022 rebound analog and strengthens the Chegg-type branch; I give that branch ~20% weight as a separate low component (median ~$180) in a mixture with a main lognormal (median ~$302, sigma 0.40). (5) The 'missed consensus ($23.72B)' guide miss was the Aug 25, 2026 guide, not a May article; the date is corrected and the claim no longer drives anything. Result: fair value $334 -> $315, P(>=268) 0.565 -> 0.535, and a fatter left tail (P(>=188) 0.825 -> 0.795) with a trimmed upper tail (P(>=469) 0.135 -> 0.115). Scenario-weighted mean ~$293; mixture mean ~$300. I remain slightly above 50% at $268 because the stock trades ~11.6x SBC-inclusive earnings with ~7.5% normalized FCF yield and heavy buybacks, and large-cap growers de-rated this hard have more often recovered than not; but the decisive evidence (the Jan-May 2027 tax season) is not yet in. Polymarket's recession figure is second-hand with volume unverified, so it is only a small left-tail input. Research in round 2 was limited to verifying the 8-K cash flow and the HRB close.
